name: NJ-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+14 partisan baseline)
Chris Smith's long incumbency and name recognition
Rachel Peace's minimal fundraising ($34K raised, $5K on hand)
Prediction markets price Smith at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: Smith holds a seat whose partisan lean favors Republicans by double digits, and his challenger has raised almost nothing to contest it. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly R+16.
model.watch: A sudden influx of outside spending against Smith or a major scandal would be the main way this race could tighten, though the district lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chris Smith, one of the longest-serving members of the House, is seeking reelection in a New Jersey district whose partisan lean favors Republicans by about fourteen points. No independent polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and market pricing.

Smith has raised about $592,000 and holds nearly $489,000 on hand, while Democrat Rachel Peace has raised roughly $34,000 with about $5,000 remaining. Prediction markets give Smith roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's lean, Smith's incumbency, and the large financial gap points to a comfortable Republican hold.
